(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a ENT Specialist / Neurologist.
(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.primary_medications: Consult a doctor for specific head maneuvers like the Epley maneuver. Avoid sudden movements.
(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.immediate_symptom_relief: Consult a doctor for specific head maneuvers like the Epley maneuver. Avoid sudden movements.
(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

AIDS.triage_action: Lifelong antiretroviral therapy (ART) and CD4/viral load monitoring under specialist care.
AIDS.primary_medications: This is a serious condition requiring lifelong antiretroviral therapy (ART) under the supervision of a healthcare professional.

Acne.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Dermatologist.
Acne.primary_medications: Maintain good skin hygiene. Use over-the-counter topical treatments with benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid. Consult a dermatologist if persistent.

Alcoholic hepatitis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Addiction Specialist.
Alcoholic hepatitis.primary_medications: Immediately stop all alcohol consumption. This is a serious condition that requires urgent medical care and a long-term management plan.
Alcoholic hepatitis.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.

Allergy.triage_action: Antihistamines, trigger avoidance. Seek urgent care if throat tightness occurs.
Allergy.primary_medications: Over-the-counter antihistamines like Cetirizine or Loratadine can help. Identify and avoid known allergens.
Allergy.immediate_symptom_relief: Over-the-counter antihistamines like Cetirizine or Loratadine can help. Identify and avoid known allergens.
Allergy.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Arthritis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Rheumatologist.
Arthritis.primary_medications: Over-the-counter pain relievers (NSAIDs like Ibuprofen). Gentle exercise and physical therapy can also help manage symptoms. Consult a doctor.

Bronchial Asthma.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Pulmonologist / Allergist.
Bronchial Asthma.primary_medications: Use prescribed inhalers as directed by your doctor. Identify and avoid triggers. Seek medical help for a long-term management plan.
Bronchial Asthma.immediate_symptom_relief: Epinephrine Inhaler (e.g., Primatene Mist - ONLY for mild, intermittent asthma and short-term use); Acetaminophen/Ibuprofen for associated pain
Bronchial Asthma.alternative_relief: N/A (Asthma requires prescription inhalers for proper control)
Bronchial Asthma.self_care_lifestyle: Avoid triggers. **Seek immediate medical attention if symptoms worsen or if breathing is severely difficult.** OTC inhalers are NOT a substitute for prescription medication.

Cervical spondylosis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Orthopedic Surgeon / Neurologist.
Cervical spondylosis.primary_medications: Gentle neck exercises, maintaining good posture, and over-the-counter pain relievers can help. Consult a doctor or physical therapist.
Cervical spondylosis.immediate_symptom_relief: Gentle neck exercises, maintaining good posture, and over-the-counter pain relievers can help. Consult a doctor or physical therapist.
Cervical spondylosis.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Chicken pox.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a General Physician / Pediatrician.
Chicken pox.primary_medications: Keep the skin cool and clean to reduce itching. Use calamine lotion or take oatmeal baths. Avoid scratching to prevent scarring.
Chicken pox.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (for fever/pain - *AVOID Ibuprofen/NSAIDs in children due to rare risk of secondary infection*)
Chicken pox.alternative_relief: Calamine Lotion or Oatmeal Baths (for itch)

Chronic cholestasis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Chronic cholestasis.primary_medications: This requires diagnosis and treatment of the underlying cause by a doctor. Do not self-medicate.
Chronic cholestasis.immediate_symptom_relief: This requires diagnosis and treatment of the underlying cause by a doctor. Do not self-medicate.
Chronic cholestasis.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Common Cold.triage_action: Supportive care, hydration, rest, OTC symptom relief.
Common Cold.primary_medications: Get plenty of rest, stay hydrated with fluids, and use over-the-counter decongestants or pain relievers for symptoms.

Dengue.triage_action: Immediate medical consultation and serial platelet monitoring required. AVOID NSAIDs/Aspirin.
Dengue.primary_medications: Rest and drink plenty of fluids. Use Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) for fever. Avoid NSAIDs like Ibuprofen and Aspirin. See a doctor immediately.
Dengue.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (for fever/pain - **ABSOLUTELY AVOID NSAIDs like Ibuprofen/Aspirin**)
contraindications_warnings: ABSOLUTELY AVOID NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Aspirin, Naproxen) as they dramatically increase internal hemorrhage/bleeding risk.

Diabetes.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Medical Specialist.
Diabetes.primary_medications: Requires a comprehensive management plan from a doctor, including diet, exercise, and possibly medication like insulin or metformin.
Diabetes.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (for general pain/fever - *check with a doctor for NSAIDs use*)
Diabetes.self_care_lifestyle: Hydration. Monitor blood sugar closely. Consult a doctor.

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Colorectal Surgeon / Proctologist.
Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).primary_medications: Increase fiber and fluid intake to soften stools. Over-the-counter creams can help with discomfort. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.
Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).immediate_symptom_relief: Increase fiber and fluid intake to soften stools. Over-the-counter creams can help with discomfort. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist.
Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Drug Reaction.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Dermatologist / Allergist.
Drug Reaction.primary_medications: Stop taking the suspected medication immediately and consult the prescribing doctor or seek emergency care if the reaction is severe.
Drug Reaction.immediate_symptom_relief: Stop taking the suspected medication immediately and consult the prescribing doctor or seek emergency care if the reaction is severe.
Drug Reaction.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Fungal infection.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Dermatologist.
Fungal infection.primary_medications: Use over-the-counter antifungal creams or powders. Keep the affected area clean and dry.
Fungal infection.immediate_symptom_relief: Use over-the-counter antifungal creams or powders. Keep the affected area clean and dry.
Fungal infection.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

GERD.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Gastroenterologist.
GERD.primary_medications: Over-the-counter antacids can provide relief. Avoid spicy, fatty foods and eating late at night. Elevate your head while sleeping.
GERD.immediate_symptom_relief: Over-the-counter antacids can provide relief. Avoid spicy, fatty foods and eating late at night. Elevate your head while sleeping.
GERD.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Gastroenteritis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Gastroenterologist / General Physician.
Gastroenteritis.primary_medications: Stay hydrated with water or oral rehydration solutions. Stick to a bland diet (bananas, rice, toast). Rest.
Gastroenteritis.immediate_symptom_relief: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) or Electrolyte Drink; Loperamide

Heart attack.triage_action: Call Emergency Medical Services (911) immediately. Do not drive.
Heart attack.primary_medications: This is a medical emergency. Call emergency services immediately. Chew an aspirin if available and recommended by emergency services.
Heart attack.immediate_symptom_relief: **EMERGENCY: Chewable Aspirin (325mg) immediately if not allergic
contraindications_warnings: CRITICAL MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Chew one adult aspirin (325mg) if not allergic, and call 911 / emergency services immediately.

Hepatitis B.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Hepatitis B.primary_medications: Requires long-term medical supervision and may involve antiviral medications prescribed by a doctor.
Hepatitis B.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.

Hepatitis C.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Hepatitis C.primary_medications: Requires treatment with antiviral medications prescribed by a specialist. Early diagnosis and treatment are key.
Hepatitis C.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.

Hepatitis D.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Hepatitis D.primary_medications: Requires management by a healthcare professional, often involving medications like interferon.
Hepatitis D.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.

Hepatitis E.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Hepatitis E.primary_medications: Primarily involves supportive care: rest, adequate nutrition, and fluids. Avoid alcohol. Usually resolves on its own.
Hepatitis E.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.

Hypertension.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Medical Specialist.
Hypertension.primary_medications: Requires lifestyle changes (low-sodium diet, exercise) and medication prescribed by a doctor. Regular blood pressure monitoring is essential.

Hyperthyroidism.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Endocrinologist.
Hyperthyroidism.primary_medications: Requires medical treatment, which may include anti-thyroid medications, radioiodine therapy, or surgery. Consult an endocrinologist.

Hypoglycemia.triage_action: Administer 15-20g fast-acting glucose immediately. If unaroused, call emergency services.
Hypoglycemia.primary_medications: Immediately consume 15-20 grams of fast-acting carbohydrates (like juice, candy, or glucose tablets). Follow up with a meal.

Hypothyroidism.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Endocrinologist.
Hypothyroidism.primary_medications: Requires daily thyroid hormone replacement medication (Levothyroxine) prescribed and monitored by a doctor.

Impetigo.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Dermatologist / Pediatrician.
Impetigo.primary_medications: This bacterial infection requires topical or oral antibiotics prescribed by a doctor. Keep the area clean and avoid touching the sores.
Impetigo.immediate_symptom_relief: This bacterial infection requires topical or oral antibiotics prescribed by a doctor. Keep the area clean and avoid touching the sores.
Impetigo.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Jaundice.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
Jaundice.primary_medications: Treatment depends on the underlying cause. It's crucial to see a doctor for diagnosis and a proper treatment plan.
Jaundice.immediate_symptom_relief: Treatment depends on the underlying cause. It's crucial to see a doctor for diagnosis and a proper treatment plan.
Jaundice.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Malaria.triage_action: Blood smear / rapid test, artemisinin-based combination therapy, hydration.
Malaria.primary_medications: Requires prescription antimalarial drugs from a doctor. Seek medical attention immediately if you suspect malaria.

Migraine.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Neurologist.
Migraine.primary_medications: Rest in a dark, quiet room. Over-the-counter pain relievers can help. For frequent migraines, a doctor can prescribe specific medications.

Osteoarthristis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Orthopedic Specialist / Rheumatologist.
Osteoarthristis.primary_medications: Maintain a healthy weight, stay active with low-impact exercises, and use over-the-counter pain relievers. Physical therapy can also help.
Osteoarthristis.immediate_symptom_relief: Maintain a healthy weight, stay active with low-impact exercises, and use over-the-counter pain relievers. Physical therapy can also help.
Osteoarthristis.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).triage_action: Urgent emergency stroke center evaluation required immediately.
Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).primary_medications: This is a medical emergency. Call emergency services immediately. Time is critical for treatment.
Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).immediate_symptom_relief: This is a medical emergency. Call emergency services immediately. Time is critical for treatment.
Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.
contraindications_warnings: TIME-CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Do not give food or fluids. Seek emergency hospital care within the golden window (<3-4.5 hours).

Peptic ulcer diseae.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Gastroenterologist.
Peptic ulcer diseae.primary_medications: Consult a qualified Gastroenterologist for a comprehensive diagnostic and medical management plan.
Peptic ulcer diseae.immediate_symptom_relief: Consult a qualified Gastroenterologist for a comprehensive diagnostic and medical management plan.
Peptic ulcer diseae.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.
contraindications_warnings: Avoid NSAIDs, aspirin, caffeine, and smoking which severely irritate the gastrointestinal mucosal lining.

Pneumonia.triage_action: Chest radiography, oxygen saturation monitoring, and prompt antibiotic/antiviral treatment needed.
Pneumonia.primary_medications: Requires antibiotics prescribed by a doctor. Get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids.
Pneumonia.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen or Ibuprofen; Dextromethorphan (Cough Suppressant); Guaifenesin (Expectorant)

Psoriasis.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Dermatologist.
Psoriasis.primary_medications: Use moisturizers and topical corticosteroids as recommended by a dermatologist. Various medical treatments are available.
Psoriasis.immediate_symptom_relief: Topical Hydrocortisone Cream (low strength); Coal Tar or Salicylic Acid products

Tuberculosis.triage_action: Chest X-ray, sputum AFB culture, and isolation precautions. Directly Observed Therapy required.
Tuberculosis.primary_medications: Consult a qualified Pulmonologist / Infectious Disease Specialist for a comprehensive diagnostic and medical management plan.
contraindications_warnings: Infectious transmission risk: Wear an N95 mask, isolate in well-ventilated space until cleared non-infectious by a physician.

Typhoid.triage_action: Blood culture, hydration, and targeted antibiotic therapy.
Typhoid.primary_medications: Requires a course of antibiotics prescribed by a doctor. Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration.

Urinary tract infection.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Urologist / Nephrologist.
Urinary tract infection.primary_medications: Drink plenty of water to help flush out bacteria. A doctor will likely prescribe a course of antibiotics.
Urinary tract infection.immediate_symptom_relief: Phenazopyridine (for pain/burning relief only - *will not cure infection*)
Urinary tract infection.self_care_lifestyle: Increased fluid intake. Requires a doctor for antibiotics.

Varicose veins.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Vascular Surgeon / Phlebologist.
Varicose veins.primary_medications: Elevate your legs when resting, wear compression stockings, and exercise regularly. A doctor can discuss other treatment options.
Varicose veins.immediate_symptom_relief: Elevate your legs when resting, wear compression stockings, and exercise regularly. A doctor can discuss other treatment options.
Varicose veins.self_care_lifestyle: Ensure adequate rest, hydration, balanced nutrition, and symptom tracking. Avoid self-prescribed antibiotics.

hepatitis A.triage_action: Schedule an in-person clinical consultation with a Hepatologist / Gastroenterologist.
hepatitis A.primary_medications: Rest, stay hydrated, and eat a healthy diet. Avoid alcohol. The body usually clears the virus on its own.
hepatitis A.immediate_symptom_relief: Acetaminophen (with extreme caution and low dose
contraindications_warnings: Strictly avoid all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances. Avoid excessive acetaminophen/paracetamol.
